To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
remyelination is variable and patient dependent.

1) the extent of remylination is variable between patients with multiple sclerosis; 2) the extent of demyelinated lesions is variable between patients; and 3) the extent of lesion remyelination is not correlated with the extent of demylination.
remyelination is extensive and occurs in the majority of patients with multiple sclerosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of remyelinating lesions and the development of a reliable method for the quantification of remyelinated tissue in the human central nervous system (CNS).
understanding the factors that influence remyelination in multiple sclerosis, with the ultimate aim of developing therapeutic approaches to enhance remyelination.
the development of a therapeutic strategy to promote remyelination in multiple sclerosis patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the extent of remission in MS is highly variable and depends on a number of factors, including age at death, disease duration and clinical course of MS.
the incidence of extensive remyelination in multiple sclerosis is not rare, but is variable and depends upon the clinical course and the duration of disease.
remyelination is a feature that is present in a significant proportion of MS patients and that its extent can be substantial.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
remyelination is a feature of the disease in a subset of MS patients.
remyelination is not only a feature of the disease process in multiple sclerosis, but it can also be a significant component of the pathology.
remyelination is a frequent and important event in the pathophysiology of multiple sclerosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the variable and often extensive extent of remyelinaiton in MS patients needs to be taken into account when designing and planning clinical trials aimed at enhancing remyelination.
the extent of remylination is variable between cases and the degree of remyelinated tissue is associated with disease duration and age at death.
the degree of remyelinating potential is variable in the global multiple sclerosis population.
